title: Ariana Grande Cancels Tonight's Seth Meyers Appearance as Focker-in-Law Countdown Hits Final Week
excerpt: Ariana Grande canceled tonight's Late Night with Seth Meyers appearance, citing a scheduling conflict, as Focker-in-Law heads toward its November 25 release.
content:
Ariana Grande has canceled her scheduled appearance on NBC's Late Night with Seth Meyers, planned for tonight, Monday, November 16, amid promotional work for her upcoming film Focker-in-Law. The cancellation was attributed to a scheduling conflict, and fans who had tickets were notified through the ticketing service 1iota that Grande would no longer take part in the taping.

Blake Griffin and Patti Harrison remained listed as the night's scheduled guests. No new date for a Grande appearance on the show has been announced.

A comeback week, interrupted

The change comes just days after Grande returned to public appearances following a two-month break. She walked the red carpet at the world premiere of Focker-in-Law on Wednesday, November 11, at the Beacon Theater in New York, alongside co-stars Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro. She also appeared on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon earlier in November as the film's release approached.

The film at the center of the week

Focker-in-Law, the fourth film in the Meet the Parents franchise, opens in theaters nationwide on Wednesday, November 25, the day before Thanksgiving. Written and directed by John Hamburg, who co-wrote the three previous films in the series, it brings back Stiller as Greg Focker and De Niro as Jack Byrnes, with Owen Wilson, Teri Polo and Blythe Danner returning in their original roles.

Grande joins the franchise as Olivia Jones, a former FBI hostage negotiator and life coach who is engaged to Henry Focker, the adult son of Greg and Pam Focker, played by Skyler Gisondo. The trailer turns on the franchise's familiar machinery: Jack subjects Olivia to the lie-detector test he once used on Greg decades earlier, and Greg, now the wary father himself, worries about where his son's relationship is heading. Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco round out the new additions to the cast.

A chart-topping fall on two fronts

The film arrives at the end of a major fall for Grande on both screen and record. Her latest album, Petal, reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200, and its lead single, “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” topped the Hot 100. The canceled Meyers appearance was to have been part of the final push before the film's Thanksgiving-week opening.

What it means

Analysis: a canceled talk-show stop nine days before a franchise release is the kind of scheduling snag studios work hard to avoid, and it is also the kind of snag that rarely matters once the opening weekend numbers arrive. Grande's return to the spotlight after two months away has been built around this one film, and the premiere, the Fallon appearance and the chart-topping album have already done most of the promotional work the Meyers slot was meant to finish. The question now is whether the absence tonight registers at all against a Thanksgiving weekend when the movie itself will be doing the talking.
